$LITE LITE CEO Michael Hurlston addressed today’s 45% selloff, pushing back on the market’s reaction.

On demand, he said there is a “massive disconnect” between the company’s demand book and what the market is pricing in, adding that “our demand couldn’t be stronger.”

When asked whether the sharp selloff gives him pause about $MRVL Marvell as the acquirer, Hurlston said the company still likes Marvell and sees significant upside from current levels one of the reasons LITE accepted an all-stock deal. He acknowledged that “the timing was bad,” but noted that the board never seriously considered anything other than an all-stock transaction after reviewing Marvell’s books and design wins.

On closing the deal (targeted for the first half of 2028), he said “it’s going to be a bumpy one,” with regulatory approval remaining the biggest remaining hurdle.
